newsitem.title: UK: Brent ends with mild losses in gas oil recovery.
newsitem.headline: Brent ends with mild losses in gas oil recovery.

text.p: IPE Brent futures posted mild losses on Tuesday but ended 40 cents off its lows with the help of gas oil in London and gasoline in New York.
Brent for November ended down 14 cts at $23.07 a barrel after slumping to a $22.67 morning low.

Gas oil led the recovery to break $235 for the first time since Gulf War hostilities in February 1991, rebounding from a shortlived test of technical support in a market driven by a mixture of speculation and sound supply-demand fundamentals.
"Fundamental demand just keeps filtering through," said one IPE broker. "A lot of people question (gas oil) prices this high but very few are prepared to go seriously short," said another.
Nervous buyers also pitched in ahead of Tuesday's latest weekly American Petroleum Institute inventory statistics, due out after the close.
Low inventories on both sides of the Atlantic have kept buyers on their toes amid fears that an early cold snap could severely stretch supply chains.
Gas oil's burst added 15 cents to its crack spread premium over crude to reach $6.90 a barrel for November contracts.
Gasoline in New York also lent support on Tuesday amid talk that a refinery fire Louisiana might shut a 50,000 bpd cat cracking unit. But operator Conoco said that operations had not been affected.
Earlier prices fell after statements from Iraq and Turkey reminded traders that a long-delayed Iraqi oil-for-food deal might get back on the rails.
But dealers remained sceptical about any rapid implementation of the exchange.
